reasoning: In Munkres 13.6, Lean evaluates `1 / 0` as 0, so K contains the positive reciprocals and their limit point 0. This K is closed in the usual topology. Removing it from an open interval leaves a usual open set, and every usual open set is lower-limit-open. This contradicts the theorem's second noncontainment claim.
